questions.q: Why is the CALCULATE-filtered MRR measure from Lesson 8 a stronger portfolio snippet than a plain SELECT * query?
options: It demonstrates understanding of the grain problem and business logic, not just DAX syntax
SELECT * is not valid DAX syntax at all
CALCULATE always runs faster than a plain SELECT
There's no real difference -- either snippet works equally well
questions.explain: Showing judgment (handling grain correctly) is more convincing to a reviewer than showing mere syntax familiarity.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what's the strongest single piece of evidence that this is a finished, working platform?
options: A link to or screenshot of the actual Power BI dashboard
The raw line count of the GitHub repository
The number of commits made to the repo
A list of every tool used, with no demonstration of them working together
questions.explain: A working dashboard is the most convincing, concrete proof the platform actually functions end to end, beyond a repo full of code.

questions.q: What answer does this lesson recommend for "what would make you distrust this dashboard's number on a given day?"
options: A specific troubleshooting order: check Airflow's run history first, then dbt test results, then query history
"I would never distrust my own dashboard's numbers"
A vague answer about "keeping an eye on things"
Immediately rebuilding the entire pipeline from scratch
questions.explain: A specific, ordered troubleshooting answer (from Lesson 12) demonstrates real operational seniority, not just technical fluency.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say the Resource Vault and Worked Examples are evidence worth mentioning in an interview?
options: They're a concrete, specific answer to "how do you keep learning beyond a course" -- a question almost every interview asks in some form
They are required reading before any interview can begin
They replace the need to discuss the actual capstone project
They are only useful for passing the course's own final test, not for interviews
questions.explain: Concrete artifacts beyond the core project -- a troubleshooting checklist, extended worked examples -- give a specific, credible answer to a very common interview question.

questions.q: Why does this lesson recommend writing the problem statement in your own words rather than copying Lesson 1's scenario verbatim?
options: A portfolio entry should reflect genuine understanding, which shows through original phrasing rather than a copied description
Copying text verbatim is technically impossible in a portfolio document
The scenario changes meaning if copied exactly
There is no stated reason -- either approach is equally recommended
questions.explain: Restating the problem in your own words signals genuine understanding of the business scenario, not just familiarity with the lesson text.
